texts.text: Limited growth on pastures due to the prolonged cooler temperatures, although warmer temperatures this week will be welcome to promote forage spring growth.

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Regional Comments
texts.text: Regional Comments

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Southwest
texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Producers have been busy harrowing low spots to help dry them out. Soil moisture levels remain somewhat high but are quickly declining due to the lack of rain and persistent high winds. Cool temperatures over the past week have begun to return to near-normal levels.
texts.text: Producers have been busy harrowing low spots to help dry them out. Soil moisture levels remain somewhat high but are quickly declining due to the lack of rain and persistent high winds. Cool temperatures over the past week have begun to return to near-normal levels.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most spring fertilizing is complete on fall seeded crops. Winter wheat and fall rye fields are greening up, but growth remains slow due to the cool conditions.
texts.text: Most spring fertilizing is complete on fall seeded crops. Winter wheat and fall rye fields are greening up, but growth remains slow due to the cool conditions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Cereal crop seeding is approximately 10 to 15 percent complete, with wheat accounting for most acres planted so far. Regions south of Highway 1 have the highest percentage completed.
texts.text: Cereal crop seeding is approximately 10 to 15 percent complete, with wheat accounting for most acres planted so far. Regions south of Highway 1 have the highest percentage completed.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pea seeding is around 40 to 50 percent complete, with early-seeded fields beginning to sprout. Corn planting is about 10 percent complete. There have been a few reports of soybeans being planted. Canola is expected to start this week.
texts.text: Pea seeding is around 40 to 50 percent complete, with early-seeded fields beginning to sprout. Corn planting is about 10 percent complete. There have been a few reports of soybeans being planted. Canola is expected to start this week.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Northwest
texts.text: Northwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The week started cool with temperatures warming slowly over the weekend. Overnight temperatures were below zero for most of the week. Snow persists in fields in The Pas and some field edges/shelterbelts in the Swan Valley. Fields in the rest of the region are mostly saturated with some standing water in low spots.
texts.text: The week started cool with temperatures warming slowly over the weekend. Overnight temperatures were below zero for most of the week. Snow persists in fields in The Pas and some field edges/shelterbelts in the Swan Valley. Fields in the rest of the region are mostly saturated with some standing water in low spots.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Warm, dry conditions are needed across the region. Limited seeding has started in the Ste. Rose/Dauphin area with select fields. Average soil temperature at most stations in the region remain cool in the single digits. Weed growth has started but has been slow with cool temperatures.
texts.text: Warm, dry conditions are needed across the region. Limited seeding has started in the Ste. Rose/Dauphin area with select fields. Average soil temperature at most stations in the region remain cool in the single digits. Weed growth has started but has been slow with cool temperatures.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Central
texts.text: Central

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Temperatures remain relatively cool across the Central Region; however dry and windy conditions over the past week have allowed for significant progress in field operations. Many producers are hoping for warmer temperatures and precipitation in the coming week to support optimum germination and early-season crop growth.
texts.text: Temperatures remain relatively cool across the Central Region; however dry and windy conditions over the past week have allowed for significant progress in field operations. Many producers are hoping for warmer temperatures and precipitation in the coming week to support optimum germination and early-season crop growth.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter wheat and fall rye survival is very good, with minimal winterkill. Fertilizer applications on winter cereals are complete. Winter cereals are at the 3-leaf stage and greening up well. However, growth is slow due to cool conditions.
texts.text: Winter wheat and fall rye survival is very good, with minimal winterkill. Fertilizer applications on winter cereals are complete. Winter cereals are at the 3-leaf stage and greening up well. However, growth is slow due to cool conditions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Manitoba Seeding of spring cereals, corn, sunflowers, and canola is well underway, while pea seeding is nearly complete. The earliest seeded pea fields are now beginning to emerge. Just over half of the spring wheat crop is seeded, and approximately 25% of the corn.
texts.text: Manitoba Seeding of spring cereals, corn, sunflowers, and canola is well underway, while pea seeding is nearly complete. The earliest seeded pea fields are now beginning to emerge. Just over half of the spring wheat crop is seeded, and approximately 25% of the corn.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola sits around 7% and sunflowers, around 15% complete. Many producers are waiting to finish corn or spring cereals before starting canola.
texts.text: Canola sits around 7% and sunflowers, around 15% complete. Many producers are waiting to finish corn or spring cereals before starting canola.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The first soybean fields were seeded last week, although most producers are waiting for warmer soil temperatures before beginning soybean seeding in earnest, as soil remains relatively cool.
texts.text: The first soybean fields were seeded last week, although most producers are waiting for warmer soil temperatures before beginning soybean seeding in earnest, as soil remains relatively cool.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Producers continue to weigh the benefits of planting early into existing soil moisture, against delaying seeding until soils warm, potentially at the expense of available moisture.
texts.text: Producers continue to weigh the benefits of planting early into existing soil moisture, against delaying seeding until soils warm, potentially at the expense of available moisture.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Eastern
texts.text: Eastern

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rainfall accumulation across the region last week, ranged from 0 to 2.8 mm with the average at 0.7 mm. Daytime temperatures early last week were cooler, with some warmer days later in the week. The current forecast for this week is for warmer temperatures as the week progresses with some rain possible earlier in the week.
texts.text: Rainfall accumulation across the region last week, ranged from 0 to 2.8 mm with the average at 0.7 mm. Daytime temperatures early last week were cooler, with some warmer days later in the week. The current forecast for this week is for warmer temperatures as the week progresses with some rain possible earlier in the week.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most areas in the region are now seeding. Manure applications are wrapping up this week. Field drains and lower areas of some fields, as well as bush-lines, continue to be too wet for equipment to pass. Producers are hopeful that the weather will warm up and that wetter fields will dry up so field operations can occur. Liquid fertilizer applications are ongoing and will continue this week.
texts.text: Most areas in the region are now seeding. Manure applications are wrapping up this week. Field drains and lower areas of some fields, as well as bush-lines, continue to be too wet for equipment to pass. Producers are hopeful that the weather will warm up and that wetter fields will dry up so field operations can occur. Liquid fertilizer applications are ongoing and will continue this week.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter cereals are looking very good with very little winter kill reported. Winter cereal fertilizer applications have wrapped up. Winter cereals are at the 3-leaf stage and are actively growing.
texts.text: Winter cereals are looking very good with very little winter kill reported. Winter cereal fertilizer applications have wrapped up. Winter cereals are at the 3-leaf stage and are actively growing.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field pea planting is underway, although there are limited acres in the region, and estimated at 75% complete.
texts.text: Field pea planting is underway, although there are limited acres in the region, and estimated at 75% complete.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Spring wheat seeding has been the focus this past week with a lot of acres completed. Total spring wheat acres seeded is estimated at 45%. Corn planting continues in the region with approximately 20% of the acres planted.
texts.text: Spring wheat seeding has been the focus this past week with a lot of acres completed. Total spring wheat acres seeded is estimated at 45%. Corn planting continues in the region with approximately 20% of the acres planted.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola seeding is just starting with total acres estimated at 5% complete across the region. Producers are focusing on other crop types before canola is seeded.
texts.text: Canola seeding is just starting with total acres estimated at 5% complete across the region. Producers are focusing on other crop types before canola is seeded.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Soybean planting is just underway in the region, with seeded acres estimated at 3%. Producers will move into planting soybeans as cereal and corn acres are finished up.
texts.text: Soybean planting is just underway in the region, with seeded acres estimated at 3%. Producers will move into planting soybeans as cereal and corn acres are finished up.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Interlake
texts.text: Interlake

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This past week overnight temperatures dipped below freezing, while daytime highs ranged from 13.1°C to 14.2°C. Rainfall varied between 0 and 1.7 mm, with average soil temperatures at seeding depth at 3.1°C. Soil moisture levels on cropland are adequate, and a small amount of snow remains visible behind the tree line in the South.
texts.text: This past week overnight temperatures dipped below freezing, while daytime highs ranged from 13.1°C to 14.2°C. Rainfall varied between 0 and 1.7 mm, with average soil temperatures at seeding depth at 3.1°C. Soil moisture levels on cropland are adequate, and a small amount of snow remains visible behind the tree line in the South.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field activity in the Interlake is steadily increasing, with fertilizer applications already in progress and some acres seeded. Soil sampling is ongoing, but cooler temperatures and wet conditions are delaying seeding for many. Operations will speed up as the weather improves.
texts.text: Field activity in the Interlake is steadily increasing, with fertilizer applications already in progress and some acres seeded. Soil sampling is ongoing, but cooler temperatures and wet conditions are delaying seeding for many. Operations will speed up as the weather improves.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Manitoba Seeding has started, and progress is expected to increase as fields get drier. As of today, spring cereals are around 10% complete in the Rockwood area, with other regions reporting corn at 5%, canola at 5%, sunflowers at 2%, and soybeans at 2%. Progress is more advanced in the South than in the North Interlake.
